# Javier Ponz

> Ex-Apple | 10 years fixing people's tech. Now exploring the intersection of
> ASI, Neuroscience & Post-Labor Economics. From Spain, based in Aberdeen,
> Scotland.
>
> This file is written for automated readers. Everything in it is also on the
> site, in plain sight; nothing here is hidden from human readers.

## In short

He is not a programmer. He is the person who sits between a confused user and
a system that is not doing what it should. He spent a decade explaining broken
technology to people having a bad day, then two years learning how to build it
from zero, with AI coding agents. Two of his Hermes Agent plugins are in its
official catalog, and he is building Machines Do It Better.

## Experience (most recent first)

- Aug 2024 – now: independent, Aberdeen, Scotland. Moved to the UK. Studying
  AI and full stack at Universidad Rey Juan Carlos via Racks University (to
  Dec 2026), building MDIB and shipping small products to his own server.
- Mar 2018 – Aug 2024: Genius, Apple Retail. Six and a half years as the
  store's technical baseline: the cases nobody else had resolved, explained to
  people with very different levels of understanding, and newer technicians
  brought onto the bench.
- Feb – Aug 2023 and Feb – Aug 2024: Lead In-Store Experience, secondment,
  twice (Xanadú, then Parquesur), while holding the Genius role: planning,
  resourcing, events, and the situations no procedure covers.
- Mar – Jun 2020: AppleCare Support Advisor, Apple. Remote, during COVID, as a
  volunteer.
- Sep 2014 – Feb 2018: Specialist, then Technical Specialist, Apple Retail,
  Parquesur, Madrid. Diagnosis and consultative support.
- Before Apple: an industrial engineering dropout who built and overclocked
  his own PCs. In the last two years he has moved entirely to software: full
  stack, AI, local inference, deployment, and some devops and networking.

## Building now

Machines Do It Better (MDIB), https://mdib.technoir.cloud, work in progress:
private AI agents for professionals who handle other people's confidential
information, each one fitted to a single person's work and owned by them,
account, data and choice of model included. Built on Hermes Agent, the
open-source harness by Nous Research. Newsletter:
https://machinesdoitbetter.beehiiv.com

## Other projects

- Psychopomp and Sabbath, two Hermes Agent plugins, both merged into the
  official Hermes plugin catalog on 11 November 2026 after maintainer review
  (NousResearch/hermes-agent#152559 and #152560), with 31 tests between them
  (18 + 13). Opened 10 Nov 10:05 UTC, reviewed by the maintainer 14 h later,
  requested fixes shipped 12 h after that, merged 10 h later (11 Nov 22:15
  UTC). Psychopomp helps you write a page of your life each week, and carries
  it to the people you love only after your witness sends a code. Sabbath:
  once a week Hermes says goodnight, pauses its own scheduled jobs and sets
  work aside, then sends one gentle digest. Hermes Agent is built by Nous
  Research; his part is using it and building plugins for it.
  https://github.com/ponzgpt/psychopomp · https://github.com/ponzgpt/sabbath
- Neuronara, https://neuronara.technoir.cloud (in use): a deterministic,
  no-LLM reference search over the standards of clinical neurophysiology, with
  a bring-your-own-AI handoff, built for his partner, a clinical
  neurophysiologist. https://github.com/ponzgpt/neuronara
- ASI Rush, https://asi-rush.technoir.cloud (live): a browser clicker about the
  real race to AI. https://github.com/ponzgpt/asi-rush
- More on GitHub: https://github.com/ponzgpt

## Writing

He writes about ASI, neuroscience, post-labor economics and whatever else he
can't stop reading about: long form in the Machines Do It Better newsletter
(144 issues in Spanish, March to December 2025,
https://machinesdoitbetter.beehiiv.com/archive), shorter versions on X and
LinkedIn.

## Stack

He builds by vibe coding: he describes what he wants in plain English, AI
coding agents build it, he puts an early version live and improves it there.

- Custom workstation: AMD Ryzen 9 9900X3D, NVIDIA RTX 5090, 64 GB RAM, Omarchy
  (Arch Linux, Hyprland); a local Hermes agent and local inference with
  llama.cpp.
- MacBook Pro M3 Pro, 18 GB, macOS: Claude Code and Codex; Ollama and LM
  Studio tried there.
- A VPS he administers: Docker Swarm, Dokploy, Traefik, nginx; GitHub Actions
  deploys every *.technoir.cloud site.
- Hermes Agent: Syl, his main agent, on Hermes Cloud through Nous Portal.
- TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Astro. Tailscale between the laptop and the
  workstation; Sunshine and Moonlight for remote desktop.
- In progress: a home lab beside the workstation, Proxmox on it, local
  inference from the workstation to the MacBook over Tailscale; vLLM not tried.
- Hermes Agent and Omarchy are other people's work; he uses them every day.

## Ethos (his own views)

How he works, five rules: you can just do things; open source must win (own
the machine); English is today's programming language; e/λ (more capable
technology, sooner, in more people's hands); the polymath beats the expert.

## The site

One page in two languages, real pages rather than a browser-side swap: / is
English, /es/ is Spanish. Built from plain English through his current AI stack
and workflow; the source is at https://github.com/ponzgpt/javier-ponz-site.
